summary: Landed the remaining phase-0-researched pension systems: CalSTRS (2%@60 / 2%@62-PEPRA age-factor tables + 30yr career factor), CalPERS (two representative tiers, since CalPERS has no single canonical formula), Texas TRS (2.3% x years x avg-5-salary with Rule-of-80 eligibility and early-retirement reduction), NYSTRS Tier 6 (tiered pension factor + anchor-point-interpolated early-reduction), Ohio STRS (unreduced path only -- the reduced/actuarial path has no published table, so it's deliberately NOT modeled and routes users to the generic fallback instead), and military Legacy High-3 / BRS (hard 20-year vesting cliff). Wired all six into simulate.js's pensionType switch, the Pension.jsx wizard step, and usePlan.js's chart labels. A Tier-4 adversarial code-review workflow (high effort) then found and all fixes were applied before commit: (1) a DRS-only survivor-reduction guard that wasn't propagated to the post-death pensEff step-down, silently zeroing non-DRS pensions after the modeled holder's death; (2) missing 'pension starts at' UI fields for military/generic, gating their year-by-year income on the stale default pensionAge=65; (3) a Texas TRS reduction-factor bug that gave a full unreduced pension to members aged 62-64 eligible only via the early path; (4) CalSTRS and CalPERS sharing one pensionTier state field with non-overlapping value domains, split into separate calstrsTier/calpersTier fields. Also added docs/sources.md §22 and a shared DEFAULT_PENSION_TYPE constant (5 duplicate 'pensionType || "drs"' call sites deduplicated).

summary: Landed the first Tier-1 international locations from phase-1's research: Mexico (Lake Chapala/Ajijic basket), Panama (Panama City basket), and Costa Rica (San Jose/Central Valley basket), each with a LOCATIONS entry (dataAsOf:2026 stamped per the widening-appeal proposal's versioning recommendation) and a matching treaty-aware INTL_TAX entry. Panama and Costa Rica are pure territorial tax systems (retireRate 0); Mexico's IRA/401(k) treaty enforcement is genuinely ambiguous per phase-1 research, modeled at a conservative 0.03 addlTaxRate. A medium-effort code-review workflow ran against the full branch diff and surfaced 2 real correctness bugs left over from phase 3 (not phase 4's own code) -- both fixed in this commit: CalSTRS's 2-at-60 tier and CalPERS (both representative tiers) computed a nonzero pension purely from the age-factor table lookup, without enforcing the minimum-years eligibility gate their own UI copy advertised (CalSTRS 50-54 age band needs 30+ years; CalPERS needs the standard 5-year vesting minimum). Added calstrsEligible/calpersEligible as the single source of truth both the formula and eligibility-note functions now defer to.

summary: Landed the final Tier 3/4 locations, completing the proposal's location roadmap: South Africa (Cape Town), Colombia (Medellin, Bogota noted as cheaper alternative), New Zealand (Auckland), and Japan (Tokyo, Osaka noted as cheaper alternative). South Africa's addition brings LOCATIONS to six continents (Europe, North America, South America, Asia, Africa, Oceania). New Zealand and Japan both carry explicit PRODUCT-HONESTY FLAGS: NZ's 'retiree visa' is a high-barrier investor product with no path to permanent residency; Japan has NO dedicated retirement visa at all (the strongest such flag in the research brief) and does NOT recognize US tax-deferred IRA/401(k) status. Also wrote docs/location-data-refresh.md, mirroring investment-data-refresh.md's pattern. A medium-effort code review then surfaced: a real docs/sources.md gap (13 new-location citations existed only inline in retirementData.js, not in the canonical sources doc -- fixed by adding sources.md section 23) and a latent NYSTRS interpolation edge case that would silently return an unreduced factor if a future data refresh desyncs NYSTRS_UNREDUCED_AGE from the anchor table's max key (fixed defensively, currently unreachable with real data). A third finding restating 'non-DRS pensions don't reduce on the holder's death' was correctly identified by the review's own refuted list as the deliberate, already-documented phase-3 design decision, not a new bug -- not touched.

summary: Cross-phase optimization pass (STEP E, all 7 phases merged). Split src/pensionData.js out of src/retirementData.js (the pension-formula constants block: DRS ERF/survivor factors through military constants) bringing retirementData.js from 564 to 426 lines, under the house 500-line guidance. Refactored Pension.jsx's 9 near-identical pensionType UI blocks into two shared components (PensionResultBox, CompensationField) -- this also fixed a real gap the earlier code reviews flagged: the 'reset to assumed' affordance previously existed only in the drs/fers blocks and was missing from the other 6 pension types. Ran /simplify (4 parallel review agents: reuse/simplification/efficiency/altitude) and fixed 2 findings: a dead `|| DEFAULT_PENSION_TYPE` fallback in isGovernmentServicePensionType (never changed the boolean outcome), and copy-paste test duplication in the new Pension.test.jsx. Also reordered the pension-type Segmented control per user request (California/Texas/New York/Ohio/Washington state systems first, then Federal/Military/Other) -- landed in phase 6. A separate ad-hoc PR (outside the phase numbering) widened the app's hero subhead beyond 'the spouse's Washington pension'/'Sofia to the Bahamas' to reflect the widened pension/location scope.
